The paper studies the scattering of plane time-harmonic electromagnetic waves by a perfectly conducting infinite cylinder.
The cylinder axis is assumed to coincide with the z-axis.
The incident wave propagates perpendicular to the cylinder axis.
Two far-field patterns are considered: FD(θ; α) for electric field and FN(θ; α) for magnetic field.
The combined far-field data set is (1 - p)FD(θ; α) + pFN(θ; α), where p is a parameter.
For 0 < p < 1, the combined far-field data set is complete in L²[−π, π] for any wave number k.
The set is incomplete if p is a transmission eigenvalue and at least one transmission eigenfunction is a Herglotz wave function.
The only possible accumulation point for values of p that make the set incomplete is p = 1/2.
The method uses a finite Fourier series to approximate the Herglotz kernel g.
The far-field pattern of uD is computed using equation (2.10) and a finite Hankel function expansion.
Tikhonov regularization is used to solve the ill-conditioned system for the coefficients of the Hankel function expansion.
The Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm is used to minimize the error functional in the reconstruction of the cylinder boundary.
The initial guess for the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm is the circle of radius one.
Reconstruction accuracy is best for p = 0 and p = 1, with a peak in error at p = 0.5.
The method remains stable even when k is close to, but not exactly at, an interior eigenvalue.
The accuracy of the reconstruction deteriorates as k approaches a Dirichlet or Neumann eigenvalue.
The paper uses synthetic data generated by solving the direct Dirichlet and Neumann scattering problems with the boundary integral equation method.
The double-layer potential approach leads to a second-kind integral equation solved by Nystrom's method with 64 equidistant grid points.
The Dirichlet solver breaks down at interior Neumann eigenvalues, and the Neumann solver breaks down at interior Dirichlet eigenvalues.
The paper investigates the same figures as in previous work for comparison, including a rounded rectangle and a kite.
The relative L₂ error in the reconstruction is used to evaluate the accuracy of the method.
The peak in error at p = 0.5 is explained by the accumulation of eigenvalues at p = 0.5.
The method does not break down unless k is very close to a Dirichlet or Neumann eigenvalue.
The paper suggests that the parameter p could be used as a new target signature in inverse scattering theory.
The potential usefulness of the new set of scattering parameters requires practical experimentation.
